sections.h2: Where to file a Wyandot County deed
sections.html:
Deeds are recorded in Room 24 of the courthouse, 109 South Sandusky Avenue, Upper Sandusky, OH 43351. That is also the mailing address. The phone is 419-294-1442, and two deputy recorders work under the elected Recorder.

Wyandot is a rural county of 21,900 people, and owners occupy 73.5 percent of occupied homes. Many parcels are farm tracts or township acreage described by section, township and range, so the legal description gets closer scrutiny here than it would for a platted city lot.

sections.h2: The Tax Map stamp comes first
sections.html:
Under the county's written conveyance standards, neither the Auditor nor the Recorder will take a deed until the Engineer's Tax Map Department has reviewed and stamped it. The stamp reads Description Checked, Tax Map Office. The department now sits in the County Engineer's office at 320 N. Warpole Street.

On an ordinary sale with an unchanged description, the reviewer follows one of four paths.

  • Approve the description as written and stamp the deed.
  • Suggest fixes for obvious typing errors, transposed numbers or rotated bearings, then stamp it.
  • Let a description with a clear point of beginning but minor flaws transfer one time, with a notice that a survey is required on the next non-exempt transfer.
  • Stamp a bad description Survey Required.

A bad description is one whose point of beginning cannot be identified or that contains an error causing ambiguity. Typical examples are missing dimensions or acreage, no section, township and range or municipality, and a parcel the grantor does not own. Deed writers are invited to have a description checked before closing, which leaves time for fixes.

sections.h2: Transfers that can skip a new survey
sections.html:
An exempt transfer, with no money paid, can move on an older description that fails today's standards, and the deed gets the survey-required notice. Exempt transfers include survivorship, family trust moves, transfers to close family, life estates, corrective deeds, court-ordered transfers, and sheriff's and auditor's deeds.

A sale for money is a non-exempt transfer. If the house stands on an acreage tract with a vague description, plan on a survey request. New splits of an existing parcel need a survey recorded in the county survey records, a closure report, and at least three working days for inspection. New parcels need 40 feet of owned highway frontage for single family housing and 60 feet for multiple family housing. Parcels that miss the 200 foot road frontage rule in the regional planning checklist must meet those minimums. Call Wyandot County Regional Planning at 419-294-4931 before you plan a split.

sections.h2: What a survey for a new lot must show
sections.html:
When an owner splits a house or acreage off a parent parcel, the survey checklist in the conveyance standards applies. Regional Planning, in Room 16 of the courthouse, reviews lots under its own rules. The checklist asks for these items:

  • A minimum property width of 200 feet and at least 1.50 acres, not counting highway right of way.
  • A lot length under four times its width.
  • Every structure, well and septic system drawn on the plat, with the distance to the nearest foot for any structure within 10 feet of a property line.
  • Required setbacks met.

Plats must be on quality bond or Mylar, at least 11 by 17 inches and in ink, so the Recorder can reproduce and microfilm them. A parent parcel divided into five or more smaller parcels is reviewed under major subdivision requirements, and earlier splits from the same parent count toward the five.

sections.h2: What Ohio law requires of the deed
sections.html:
Under Revised Code 5301.01 the grantor signs and has the signature acknowledged by an authorized officer, usually a notary. Revised Code 317.13 has the Recorder log each instrument with its date and the minute it arrived, so filing order settles priority.

The same section lets a recorder turn down a paper the Code does not authorize or one that looks fraudulent, and the filer has a court remedy. It also calls for electronic recording and online indexes reaching back to 1980. Ask the Wyandot office which electronic options it offers.

Most sales owe it, and the seller pays. Revised Code 319.54 states the fee as one dollar or ten cents per hundred dollars, whichever is greater, and Revised Code 319.202 has the buyer file a statement of value first. In a sale, value is the whole consideration, with any mortgage on the property counted in.

Which transfers owe the conveyance fee
Type of transferConveyance fee
Gift between spouses, or parent and childNot charged
Among heirs or devisees of one decedent, no money paidNot charged
Into a trust the grantor can revokeNot charged
To confirm or correct a recorded deedNot charged
Sale to a buyer for moneyCharged at the rate above

The statute lists more exemptions, such as court ordered transfers that are not sales. Revised Code 322.02 also lets a county levy its own transfer tax, so ask the Wyandot County Auditor whether one applies.

The page-based charges in Revised Code 317.32 are the same statewide, and the Recorder can quote your total. A long metes and bounds description adds pages, so ask before you mail the deed.

Pull the previous deed before the new one is typed. A new metes and bounds description must cite the prior deed and the source of each exception, and the acreage must be shown to three decimal places. A tract may carry no more than four exceptions.

sections.h2: Steps for a seller before closing
sections.html:
Start early on a rural parcel. Pull the last recorded deed and the tax map, then take the draft deed to the Tax Map Department for a description check before the closing date. If the stamp comes back Survey Required, you have time to hire a surveyor, where a stamp discovered on closing day could delay the sale.

A cash buyer does not wait on a lender's appraisal, but the Tax Map stamp, the Auditor's fee and the Recorder's filing all still apply. After the deed is stamped and the fee is paid, take it to Room 24 for filing.

sections.h2: Researching a parcel before you list
sections.html:
The Tax Map Department also helps the public find property, check ownership and obtain new addresses in unincorporated areas. Its county page offers downloads of tax maps, property surveys and legal descriptions, plus a current parcel data file in ZIP format that the county supplies as is. The County Auditor keeps an online tax map site as well.

An owner with an older farm or edge-of-town house can collect three items early:

  • The parcel number and acreage the Auditor shows on the tax map.
  • The last recorded deed, with its legal description and any exceptions.
  • Any recorded survey for the tract, which settles whether a survey will be demanded on the next transfer.

Compare the deed acreage with the tax map. For older descriptions that are not metes and bounds, the standards tolerate a difference of only 0.2 acre on parcels under 5 acres and 5 percent on larger ones.

faqs.q: Is a survey required for a Wyandot County house?
faqs.a: Sometimes. A sale with an unchanged description moves after the Tax Map stamp. A bad description earns a Survey Required stamp, and any split of a parcel needs a recorded survey.

faqs.q: Where is the Wyandot County Tax Map Department?
faqs.a: It operates from the County Engineer's office at 320 N. Warpole Street in Upper Sandusky.

faqs.q: Who covers the Auditor's fee in Wyandot County?
faqs.a: The seller. The statute measures it at the greater of one dollar or ten cents per hundred dollars of value.

faqs.q: How do I reach the Wyandot County Recorder?
faqs.a: Phone 419-294-1442, or visit Room 24 of the courthouse at 109 South Sandusky Avenue.

faqs.q: Can a deed be turned away?
faqs.a: Yes, if the paper is not authorized for recording or looks fraudulent. The filer can go to court to seek an order.
